name: Why Schemas Matter
title: Why Schemas Matter
description: Schemas turn freeform instructions into structured data that tools can validate, search, combine, and execute. Without a schema, every recipe is an island; with one, recipes become a library.
how_it_works: Define the fixed structure (fields, types, required vs optional) for build recipes in your domain. Validate every recipe against the schema before accepting it into the library.
key_points: Schemas make recipes validatable, searchable, combinable.
Validate before accepting into the library.

standards: Data schema design practice (JSON Schema, versioning); recipe documentation conventions.
citations: JSON Schema specification - structuring and validating recipe data.

name: Required vs Optional Fields
title: Required vs Optional Fields
description: Required fields guarantee the minimum viable recipe; optional fields allow richness. Too many required fields strangle contributors; too few produce useless recipes.
how_it_works: Mark required only what every recipe needs to be buildable (title, steps, materials); keep the rest optional. Review the split as the library grows - promote fields that prove universally useful.
key_points: Review the split as the library grows.
requirements: Defined recipe elements (ingredients/materials, steps, parameters, checks); schema versioning; validation rules.

name: Data Types in Schemas

how_it_works: Assign types deliberately: quantities as number+unit pairs, durations as numbers with time units, references as IDs not names. Validate types on entry - 'about 5' is not a number.
key_points: Quantities: number plus unit, never bare strings.

Stability is a promise; versioning keeps it.
